name: wtx (gRPC server)
workload: Unary gRPC call over plaintext HTTP/2 with protobuf, 256 and 1024 held connections, 5s runs, on the HttpArena multi-language benchmark harness
claimed_speedup: 3.7-5.5x higher req/s than grpc-go: 3,990,708 vs 720,798 rps at 256 conns (avg latency 6.55ms vs 35.14ms); 3,620,970 vs 969,718 rps at 1024 conns (avg latency 26.89ms vs 88.65ms) (derived from page data)
compiler_and_flags: Rust nightly-2026-06-27, `cargo build --release` with `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"` (per frameworks/wtx-grpc/Dockerfile in MDA2AV/HttpArena); grpc-go built with the standard Go toolchain (frameworks/grpc-go in the same repo)
hardware: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX, 64 dedicated cores, stated as identical conditions for every framework (HttpArena methodology docs)
tradeoffs: wtx is a multi-protocol crate (gRPC, HTTP/2, WebSocket, Postgres, TLS, etc.) rather than a dedicated RPC-only library; requires nightly Rust; small community and, per its own README, 'not widely used and has not undergone security audits'; used noticeably more memory (727MiB-1022MiB) than grpc-go (310-922MiB) in this test.
caveats: wtx's server process used ~64 CPU-equivalent cores (6379-6383% cpu) versus grpc-go's ~44 (4339-4478% cpu) during the run, so throughput-per-core is not directly comparable, only end-to-end rps on shared hardware. The harness (HttpArena, github.com/MDA2AV/HttpArena, MIT-licensed) is a general full-stack web-framework benchmark, not an RPC-specific shootout, and the wtx-grpc entry appears to have been contributed by wtx's own author as one of ~150 framework entries, so it is not a fully arms-length third party -- though the Dockerfiles, build commands and raw JSON results are public and run centrally by the HttpArena maintainers alongside every other entry under the same load generator. A tonic (Rust's official gRPC framework) directory exists in the same repo but did not appear in the published results table at the time of access, so a same-language comparison against Rust's own gRPC stack was not confirmed.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): LesnyRumcajs/grpc_bench README -> rust_wtx_bench directory -> c410-f3r/wtx README 'High-level benchmarks' link -> https://www.http-arena.com/ -> https://www.http-arena.com/data.json (profiles unary-grpc-256, unary-grpc-1024)

name: cmd-stream-go (MUS/protobuf TCP transport)
workload: Echo RPC benchmark with 1/2/4/8/16 concurrent Go client goroutines, 17-1024 byte payloads, 30ms artificial server delay, plain TCP transport; `go test -bench BenchmarkQPS`
claimed_speedup: At 16 concurrent clients: cmd-stream over TCP with MUS serialization reached 288,727 qps vs grpc's 63,285 qps (~4.6x); cmd-stream with protobuf serialization reached 220,338 qps (~3.5x) at the same concurrency (derived from page data: results/qps/qps.csv)
compiler_and_flags: Go 1.24.1, default `go test -bench` build; no explicit optimization flags stated
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U laptop, Debian 6.1.148-1 x86_64, run on AC power with fan at full speed (per repo README)
tradeoffs: Requires the MUS binary codec (or protobuf) and cmd-stream's own client/server API instead of generated gRPC stubs; much smaller ecosystem, tooling and cross-language support than gRPC; the same benchmark suite also tested DRPC and Kitex, which did not beat gRPC under these conditions.
caveats: The benchmark's author, ymz-ncnk, also maintains the MUS serialization format (mus-go/mus-format, itself already catalogued) and is affiliated with the cmd-stream project, so this is not a fully independent third party. It is a single-laptop run (not a dedicated benchmark server) with `-count=10` repetitions but no multi-machine or cross-run statistical analysis, and the author notes thermal/power caveats. cmd-stream-go is already catalogued separately; this entry is reported only as fresh independent-style benchmark evidence for it.
